subject: Dimension discrepancies between theme_bw and theme_grey

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Dimension discrepancies between theme_bw and theme_grey
parts:
I've been making some graphs for print output and I've had some issues with the defaults for theme_bw. Specifically, the x-axis label is a bit high and tends to crowd the tick marker labels. When I use theme_grey, this hasn't been an issue.

Here's some code that illustrates:

library(ggplot2)

data <- data.frame(x=rnorm(20), y=rnorm(20))
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + xlab("My x-axis label") + ylab("My y-axis label")

p + theme_grey() # Good
p + theme_bw()   # Not so good


It appears that theme_grey and theme_bw have different default values for the vjust of axis.title.x. The label crowding can be fixed by setting the value, but it seems to me that one shouldn't have to do this just to get a decent-looking graph.
p + theme_bw() + opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(vjust=0.5))


There are other visual differences. Here are the ones that I can see:
- Axis labels too close with theme_bw
- Tick labels are further from axis with theme_bw
- Drawing area is slightly larger with theme_grey

Overall, the axis and tick labels look better to my eye with theme_grey.


I took a closer look at the definitions for theme_bw and theme_grey, and I found some other discrepancies in dimensions. Here's a summary of the differences I found:

theme_grey: axis.ticks = theme_segment()
theme_bw:   axis.ticks = theme_segment(size = 0.2)

theme_grey: axis.title.x = theme_text(vjust = 0.5)
theme_bw:   axis.title.x = theme_text(vjust = 1)

theme_grey: axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm")
theme_bw:   axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "lines")

theme_grey: axis.ticks.margin = unit(0.1, "cm")
theme_bw:   axis.ticks.margin = unit(0.5, "lines")

theme_grey: panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "white")
theme_bw:   panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "grey90", size = 0.2)

theme_grey: panel.grid.minor = theme_line(colour = "grey95", size = 0.25)
theme_bw:   panel.grid.minor = theme_line(colour = "grey98", size = 0.5)


Different line weights for the grid make sense to me (although I'm not sure why the major gridline thickness is defined for one but not the other), but it's not clear to me why the other differences should be there. Are these differences intentional?
